existing_localTerm:

existing_standing:
The 1996 'three plus or minus' formula puts the mother tongue as medium

existing_mediumOfInstruction:
2013 Education Act: English is the medium of instruction in schools and colleges

existing_taughtAsSubject: Not established from the sources consulted. The UNESCO PEER inclusion profile for Malawi covers Chichewa only as a permitted medium under the 2013 Education Act, and notes nationwide Chichewa textbook distribution plus piloted mother-tongue projects awaiting scale-up; it describes no timetabled Malawian-language subject, no year range and no optionality. existing_localTerm:

Fixed in the Constitution of 1996, art. 9: a law sets their promotion and development

existing_standing:
Recognised as national languages; only French and Arabic are official (Constitution art. 9)
Art. 9(2) leaves their promotion and development to be fixed by law
Loi d'orientation du système éducatif (2006) art. 5: teaching may also be given in them

existing_mediumOfInstruction:
2006 orientation law: teaching may also be given in the national languages
Primary is delivered in the official languages and also in the national languages

Leclerc: nearly all classes for children and young people are given in French or Arabic
existing_taughtAsSubject:
2006 law names foreign languages as subjects, national languages only as media
A Direction de la promotion des langues nationales monitors teaching programmes in them
Its named programme work is literacy and non-formal education in those languages

existing_localTerm:

existing_standing:
English and Sesotho are both official under the Constitution, Chapter 1, Section 3
